scenes.title: Read the protected .aws canary
scenes.description: Request one public canary file. The native conversation reports that the path does not exist.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual native macOS client request and recorded assistant summary of the fs_read error. Host fixture existence and namespace masking require the separate verification receipt; this clip does not show a governance-hook denial.

source.description: Actual native KiroCrew Nightly window on macOS, connected to the existing EC2 Gateway and original Kiro CLI.

cues.label: Request the public canary
cues.detail: The request names one prepared public file under /home/crew/.aws; no credentials, directory listing or retry is requested.

cues.label: Submit the read
cues.detail: The native client submits the single-file request to the EC2 session.

cues.label: Inspect the reported read error
cues.detail: The assistant reports that fs_read returned a path-does-not-exist error. Correlate this summary with the native tool event and host namespace receipt.

scenes.title: Try writing a protected configuration path
scenes.description: Request one disposable marker beneath the protected agent configuration directory and observe the blocked-tool notice.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual native macOS client request, safety-policy blocked notice and assistant summary. The exact write-protection gate and target absence are verified separately. The product displays both a 1 file changed heading and a no changes row.

source.description: Actual native KiroCrew Nightly window on macOS, connected to the existing EC2 Gateway and original Kiro CLI.

cues.label: Request the disposable marker
cues.detail: The request names the prepared disposable target under /home/crew/.kiro/agents/.demo-host-controls and specifies one public marker.

cues.label: See the native block
cues.detail: The product displays Tool call blocked and states that a safety policy blocked the call.

cues.label: Inspect the write result
cues.detail: The assistant names the write-protected-config-path gate. The product also displays 1 file changed with no changes; use the separate host receipt for target absence.

scenes.title: Approve an IMDS TCP probe
scenes.description: Approve inspection of the public helper, approve its execution once, then inspect the failed TCP result.
scenes.evidenceScope: Actual native macOS client request, separate source-read and execution approvals, and recorded assistant summary: connected false, errno 113, zero application bytes and no metadata requested. Attribution to the UID firewall rule requires separate host counter evidence; the assistant wording does not establish that the whole host lacks an IMDS route.

source.description: Actual native KiroCrew Nightly window on macOS, connected to the existing EC2 Gateway and original Kiro CLI.

cues.label: Request the TCP-only probe
cues.detail: The request names the reviewed public helper, with no extra arguments, HTTP request, metadata request or retry.

cues.label: Inspect the helper approval
cues.detail: The client asks permission to read the public helper before execution. The recording retains this separate Allow once decision.

cues.label: Inspect the execution approval
cues.detail: The client requests a second Allow once decision for the exact helper command. Approval permits execution; it does not remove the host network control.

cues.label: Inspect the failed TCP result
cues.detail: The assistant reports connected false, errno 113, zero application bytes and no metadata requested. The native tool event and separate host counters establish the supported attribution; the whole-host routing claim is not adopted.
